solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Type of tweed nothing new for Beatle

parts.note: the hand-woven cloth from the Outer Hebrides island of that name

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a tweed jacket to suit one of the Fab Four.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris tweed is a hand-woven Scottish cloth, which is why 'Type of tweed' gives HARRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: George, the lead guitarist, is one member of the Beatles.

clue.text: Crowd keen to consume seconds …

indicators.note: to consume food is to take it inside you, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: hot = keen, eager, as in hot on a subject

explanation.surface: An eager diner wolfs down second helpings, leading on to the meat in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like second helpings at the table; it is just the unit abbreviation S. The ellipsis joins this clue to 2 down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a large number of people, as in 'a heavenly multitude' or 'a whole army of fans'.

clue.text: … cooked meat in pan

definitions.meaning: a joint done in the oven, the centre of a Sunday lunch
the verb: to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does a bad show

explanation.surface: The keen diner's seconds turn out to be meat cooked in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like the cooking vessel, which suits the meat; it is the critic's verb, and a savage review is a ROAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a joint of meat cooked in the oven, and the informal verb for tearing someone apart in public.

clue.text: Drunk man from Italy likely to cause trouble

indicators.note: a drunk staggers and lurches, so the letters that follow are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An inebriated Italian is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' sits at the front as an adjective describing the man, so it reads as part of the picture rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: words that inflame feelings stir people up and so are likely to cause trouble.

clue.text: Old stove in Dutch royal house

parts.note: a large kitchen stove, often cast iron and kept alight all day

explanation.surface: An antique stove stands in a Dutch palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building to put the stove in; it means a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the Netherlands is ruled by the House of Orange-Nassau, the dynasty of William of Orange.

clue.text: Court order fans abhor regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Supporters hate a ruling from the court, perhaps one banning them from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order restricting a nuisance's conduct, often handed to football hooligans.
explanation.definitionFit: Acronym: the Anti-Social Behaviour Order was a UK civil order made by a court.

clue.text: Wise importing Australia's food

indicators.note: to import goods is to bring them in, so one piece is carried inside the other

parts.note: the first three letters of Australia, a truncation

explanation.surface: A shrewd trader brings in Australian produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Importing' fits the trade picture of food shipped from Australia; in the wordplay it only asks one piece to carry another.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a banger, the thing on the barbecue, is one kind of food.

clue.text: French pop in over-the-top American musical work

indicators.note: one piece is put in another, inside it

parts.note: père is French for father, dad, pop

explanation.surface: A French pop song finds its way into an overblown American musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French pop' looks like chart music from Paris; pop here is a father, and the French for that is père.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a light opera with spoken dialogue, such as Gilbert and Sullivan wrote, is a musical work.

clue.text: Any date's sure to change for movable feast!

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters, with the 's giving an S

explanation.surface: The date of a movable feast is bound to shift from year to year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true of the answer: the festival's date changes every year, set by the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Church term: a movable feast is one whose date varies year to year, and this one follows the first full moon after the spring equinox.

clue.text: Stick man

definitions.meaning: a long walking stick or rod
the verb: to provide with workers, as in man a desk

explanation.surface: A stick figure, the simplest drawing of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick man' reads as a child's drawing; split it, and 'man' is a verb meaning to put people to work somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a shepherd's or wizard's rod, and the verb for supplying a place with workers.

clue.text: Usually like beer taking in rugby

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the beer surrounds the rugby

explanation.surface: Someone who normally enjoys a beer while taking in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in' suggests watching a match; it is a container instruction. Rugby Union is the fifteen-a-side code of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means generally, in the normal run of things.

clue.text: Keep this and give nothing away

definitions.text: Keep this and give nothing away

parts.note: reads as holding on to a possession; really it is keeping an expression fixed on your face
reads as refusing to share; really it is revealing none of your feelings

explanation.surface: A miser's rule: hang on to this and never share anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give nothing away' sounds like meanness with possessions; it means betraying no emotion, and 'keep' is the verb the idiom uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: you keep a composed, unsmiling expression so as not to reveal your feelings or laugh.

clue.text: 100 among Bedouin somehow stranded in Arctic?

indicators.note: one thing among others is placed within them
in some unstated way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred desert nomads find themselves improbably stuck at the Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The C goes among the jumbled letters of BEDOUIN. The question mark flags a definition by example: the Arctic is only one place a ship can be frozen in.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: held fast by ice, as a ship caught in Arctic pack ice is.

clue.text: Support feature in newspaper

definitions.meaning: a pillar holding up a roof
a regular article by one writer

explanation.surface: An article in the paper backing a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' reads as backing an idea, which a newspaper piece might do; it is the architectural pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an upright pillar that holds up a structure, and a regular slot for one writer in a paper.

clue.text: Pound is small housing single feline

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside

parts.note: L = pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: An animal pound is too small to hold even one cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the animal shelter; it is the currency sign L. IS and S join as ISS, which houses ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the female big cat is one member of the feline family.

clue.text: Burning paintings outside study

indicators.note: one piece stands outside another, wrapping round it

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: Pictures go up in flames outside someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' seems to describe the paintings on fire; it is the definition, in its passionate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: from the Latin for 'burning', it now mostly means passionately keen, as in a burning desire.

clue.text: Complaint from mum after time in volcanic dust

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer
one piece is put in another, inside it

explanation.surface: Breathing trouble caused by volcanic dust.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible: volcanic ash does bring on breathing attacks. 'Complaint' is medical, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a chronic breathing condition is a complaint in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Our boss with a turn fixed old browser

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired, its parts put back in a new order

explanation.surface: The boss takes a turn at fixing an out-of-date web browser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old browser' looks like software; a browser is also an animal that grazes on leaves, and this one is a dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: a huge plant-eating dinosaur, an ancient animal that browsed on vegetation.

clue.text: Shadow inside Museum Brandhorst

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last two letters of Museum and first three of Brandhorst

explanation.surface: A shadow falls inside a Munich art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Museum Brandhorst is a modern art gallery in Munich; only its name matters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: Latin for shadow, used in astronomy for the darkest part of an eclipse shadow.

clue.text: Here you might see stallion bolt

definitions.meaning: a farm where stallions are kept for breeding
a short threaded rod or rivet

explanation.surface: A horse breaking loose at the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like the stallion running off; it is the hardware sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a breeding farm where you would find stallions, and a short metal rod or rivet.

clue.text: Discover tofu near the sandwiches

indicators.note: outer words sandwich the answer, holding it between them like bread

parts.note: the last letter of tofu, all of near, and the first two letters of the

explanation.surface: Finding tofu tucked into someone's sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food to go with the tofu; it is the verb, holding the answer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: literally to dig up out of the ground, and so to find something hidden.

clue.text: Account subtraction in notes and coin

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
a small coin, as in the old British threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Money taken out of an account, paid in banknotes and coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like banknotes; here they are musical notes. A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting term: an entry recording a sum taken out, the opposite of a credit.

clue.text: Food hamper's first on Pluto

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another follows it

explanation.surface: A hamper of food sent into space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' looks like the dwarf planet; it is the god of the underworld, also called Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a prepared item of food, as on a menu.

clue.text: Spoil Dylan broadcast in US state

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A bad radio broadcast of a Bob Dylan concert in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the radio picture; its older sense is scattering seed, which is why it jumbles DYLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the state on Chesapeake Bay, capital Annapolis, is one of the fifty.
